reason: The only production Bash constructor is process/worker.mjs with python:false; the shell command allowlist omits python and python3. This is not a promise about arbitrary use of the private Bash library API.
The fixed production shell command allowlist omits sqlite3. Node built-in node:sqlite remains separately available.
The production Bash constructor has javascript:false; js-exec and the upstream node stub are not used. The separately registered Node command uses the approved real Worker.
The production Bash constructor never supplies coverage. The development flag-coverage collector imports SQLite metadata and is entirely omitted with it.

The fixed production shellCommands never registers tar; actual shell invocations already return 127 with a desktop alternative. Its archive codec chunk is referenced only by this omitted tar entry and omitted development flag coverage.
The fixed filesystem implementation enters Win32 ACL helpers only when process.platform is win32; OHOS takes the POSIX/publication branch.
The fixed driver selector creates the Windows dialog/abort path only for win32; OHOS does not start that dialog worker.
This is the Win32 dialog worker, started only by the win32 driver selector. Arbitrarily importing this private worker is outside the product entrypoint contract.
convertBytes throws the explicit OHOS unavailable error before constructing or loading the converter; tested through its real consumer.
The fixed session implementation selects Win32 semaphore/MoveFileEx only for win32; OHOS uses the linked publication owner and main-thread lock path.
Win32 helpers in this worker are selected only by its fixed platform branches; OHOS does not enter them.
getRgPath returns the virtual rg token immediately on openharmony, before the native binary import; the actual strict grep round covers this path.
The OH-only patch throws OHOS_PROXY_NEGOTIATE_UNAVAILABLE before this import on openharmony; real hook invocation is covered by the composition test.
